To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the base current is reduced by the use of Ti-Au over Au-Zn-Au base metallization scheme and by the use of the δ+ composite collector structure, 2) the current gain of the circular geometry InGa/AlAs DHBTs is 50 for 94.5 μm spacing and 100 for 5.5 μm and 3) the collector leakage current is reduced by a factor of 1000 by the use of δ+-
the collector leakage current can be reduced to a value of less than 1% of the collector current by the use of the novel composite collector structure.
the collector leakage current in InGaP/GaN double heterojunction transistors is reduced by 2-3 orders of magnitude by the use of a δ+-layer composite structure in the collector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of base-collector leakage current in circular geometry InP/InGaAs/InGaP double heterojunctions.
a new approach to the fabrication of circular geometry InGaAs/InGaP DHBT's.
the development of a novel δ+-layer composite-collector InGaP/GaN HBT structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the base current in circular geometry devices can be minimized to the intrinsic value by using a proper base metallization scheme.
the base–collector leakage currents are due to the presence of an inversion layer in the collector region.

the collector leakage current is not the dominant leakage current component in circular geometry In0.5Al0.5As/InP DHBTs and that it is the surface recombination leakage current which is the dominant leakage current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the δ+-layer collector structure reduces the collector leakage current by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude as compared to the conventional collector structure.
the base-collector leakage current is a function of the spacing between the base metal pad and emitter mesa.
the collector leakage current is reduced by a factor of 10 for the 5.5 and 10.5 µm devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the base–collector leakage current is not a significant factor in the performance of the device as it is in a conventional collector structure.
with a δ+-layer composite structure, the collector current is independent of collector spacing and the collector leakage current is independent of base spacing.
a reduction in the collector leakage current is possible by increasing the collector doping concentration.
